items.title: feat(auth): set default host on login to a self-managed instance
items.body:
## Description

After `glab auth login` succeeds for an instance other than gitlab.com, glab updates the global `host` key. Commands run outside a Git repository, such as `glab repo clone`, then reach that instance instead of gitlab.com.

- If the default is still `gitlab.com` and gitlab.com has no stored credentials, glab sets `host` and prints `Default instance set to <host>`.
- If gitlab.com has credentials, or a different default has been set, glab asks first in interactive mode. In scripted mode, it prints `glab config set --global host <host>` instead.
- Skipped in CI and when `GITLAB_HOST`, `GITLAB_URI`, or `GL_HOST` is set. Skipped for `--job-token` logins.

## Related Issues

Resolves #310

## How has this been tested?

- `go test ./internal/commands/auth/login/...` passes.
- New `Test_tokenLogin_updatesDefaultHost` covers every case through the `--token` path.

items.title: fix(label): show the real total in the list header
items.body:
## Description

`glab label list` passed `len(labels)` as both the count and the total in its
header, so the total was always the size of the current page. A project with 33
labels showed `Showing label 30 of 30` with the default page size, and
`3 of 3` on page 2.

This keeps the `*gitlab.Response` returned by `ListLabels` and
`ListGroupLabels`, and prints `resp.TotalItems` as the total. When the
response carries no total (GitLab omits `X-Total` for very large result sets,
and the existing tests mock a `nil` response), it falls back to the page count,
which is the current behavior.

The table body and the JSON output are unchanged.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8573

Related to #1165, which covers list commands that print no total at all.

## How has this been tested?

- Added a project case and a group case to
  `internal/commands/label/list/label_list_test.go` that mock a response with
  `TotalItems: 33`. Both fail on `main` with `2 of 2` / `1 of 1` and pass with
  this change. The existing cases, which mock a `nil` response, still pass.
- `go test ./internal/commands/label/...` passes.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/commands/label/...` (v2.14.0, as pinned in
  `.tool-versions`) reports 0 issues, and `golangci-lint fmt --diff` reports no
  changes.
- `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap` reports 0 findings on the changed files.
- Ran a build of this branch against a self-managed GitLab 19.3.3-ee project
  with 33 labels:

  | Command | `main` | This branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `glab label list` | `30 of 30` | `30 of 33` |
  | `glab label list -p 2` | `3 of 3` | `3 of 33` |
  | `glab label list -P 10` | `10 of 10` | `10 of 33` |
  | `glab label list -g GROUP` | `30 of 30` | `30 of 33` |

  The table body and `-F json` output are byte-identical to `main`.

items.title: ci(release): render Slack release notes as markdown
items.body:
## What

Improves the release announcement goreleaser posts to Slack, and tidies the release notes it generates.

### Slack post

- Release notes go in a Slack `markdown` block, so headings, bold text and links render instead of showing raw `##`/`###` markdown.
- The extra `## Changelog` heading is dropped.
- Each line ends with an emoji for the commit author type:
  - 🤖 for `gitlab-bot@gitlab.com`
  - `:tanuki:` for other `@gitlab.com` authors
  - `:community:` for everyone else
- Notes are cut at 10,000 characters and end with `…`, which keeps them under Slack's 12,000-character limit for a markdown block.
- `message_template` is now a short plain-text fallback for notification previews.
- `icon_emoji` is `:glab:` to match the bot's existing avatar.
- The pre-release warning and `release.prerelease: auto` are removed. goreleaser ignores that setting for GitLab releases, and the last pre-release tag was `v1.20.0-pre1`.

### Changelog lines (Slack and GitLab release page)

- Author emails are dropped, and each commit SHA links to the commit.
- The `type(scope):` prefix is bold. Messages whose prefix contains a space, such as `Revert "…"`, are left alone.
- Maintenance is listed above Dependencies. The Dependencies group stays first in the config so it still claims the `chore(deps)` commits.
- Author-type markers are written as HTML comments (`<!--team-->` etc.). GitLab doesn't display them, so the release page has no author emojis. The Slack template swaps them for the emojis.

Example line:

```
* **feat(df):** add package command to check a single PURL ([c81a40c8](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/commit/c81a40c8)) by Michael Eddington :tanuki:
```

## Why

The current post sends markdown as plain Slack text, so headings show up literally and every line includes an email address. This is based on the gitlab-lsp release post.

## Testing

- `goreleaser check` passes.
- Rendered the changelog format and Slack block templates against the v1.120.0 commits with a local copy of goreleaser's template functions. Also tested a `Revert "…"` message, a message with a second `: `, and the 10,000-character cut-off.
- Checked with GitLab's markdown API that the HTML comment markers aren't displayed.
- Previewed the Slack block in Block Kit Builder. Not posted to a real webhook, so the first release after merge is the end-to-end check.

issue.title: Add a way to close milestones
issue.body:
### Problem to solve

Right now you can do the basic CRUD operations on milestones, but you can not close them.

### Proposal

Add a new flag: `glab milestone edit XXX --close` that would close the given milestone.

### Further details

Our milestones work on a time based, so whenever the period finishes, we create new milestones, move open work items to the these new milestones and finally we close the old milestones.

So far we can do all of it but the last part, closing milestones.

items.title: Move pending review comments to `glab mr note draft` subcommands
items.body:
### Problem to solve

Pending review comments (draft notes) are currently exposed as a `--draft` flag on the existing `glab mr note` verbs, plus a separate `publish` verb:

| Action | Today | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | `glab mr note create --draft` | Merged in !3885, released in v1.119.0 |
| Publish | `glab mr note publish` | Merged in !3909, released in v1.120.0 |
| List | `glab mr note list --draft` | Proposed in !3963 (#8563) |
| Discard | `glab mr note delete --draft <id>` | Proposed in !3963 (#8563) |
| Edit | `glab mr note update --draft <id>` | Proposed in #8569 |

Draft notes are a different GitLab resource with a different API (`/merge_requests/:iid/draft_notes`, `DraftNotesService` in client-go) than published notes and discussions. Overloading every `mr note` verb with `--draft` has these costs:

- Every verb branches on `--draft` into a separate code path, with its own client calls, output format, and error messages. `create` already has to dispatch `--draft` before `--reply`, and `list`/`delete`/`update` would each need a parallel implementation (!3963 adds `runDraft`, `completeDraft`, and a separate printer).
- Flag matrices grow. `--draft` must be rejected with `--unique`, `--resolvable=false`, and `--internal` on `create`, and with `--type` and `--state` on `list`. Each rule needs validation code, help text, and tests.
- The ID namespace changes under the same command: `glab mr note delete 123 456` deletes note 456, while `glab mr note delete --draft 123 456` deletes draft note 456.
- `--draft` already means "draft merge request" on `glab mr create`, `glab mr update`, and `glab mr list`. `glab mr list --draft` and `glab mr note list --draft` would filter completely different things.
- The publish step lives at `glab mr note publish`, detached from the commands that manage what it publishes.

Discussed in !3885 (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3885#note_3928426677) and agreed by @viktomas, @phikai, and @andrei.zubov. This is the shape used by the original POC (!2932) and by https://gitlab.com/viktomas/note.

### Proposal

Add a `draft` noun under `glab mr note` that owns the full pending review lifecycle, and remove the flag-based commands:

```shell
glab mr note draft create  [<id> | <branch>] [-m <body>] [--file <path> [--line N[:M] | --old-line N]] [--reply <discussion-id>] [--attach <file>]
glab mr note draft list    [<id> | <branch>] [--file <path>] [-F json]
glab mr note draft update  [<id> | <branch>] <draft-note-id> [-m <body>] [--attach <file>]
glab mr note draft delete  [<id> | <branch>] <draft-note-id> [--yes]
glab mr note draft publish [<id> | <branch>] [-m <summary>] [--internal] [--reviewer-state requested_changes|reviewed] [--yes]
```

Mapping from the current and proposed commands:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `glab mr note create --draft` | `glab mr note draft create` |
| `glab mr note publish` | `glab mr note draft publish` |
| `glab mr note list --draft` (!3963) | `glab mr note draft list` |
| `glab mr note delete --draft` (!3963) | `glab mr note draft delete` |
| `glab mr note update --draft` (#8569) | `glab mr note draft update` |

Behavior carried over unchanged:

- `draft create`: same diff targeting (`--file`, `--line`, `--old-line`), same `--reply` prefix resolution, same `--attach` behavior, and the success output stays the bare draft note ID so it can be piped into `draft update` and `draft delete`. Flags that never applied to drafts (`--unique`, `--resolvable`, `--internal`) do not exist on the new command, so their conflict rules and tests go away.
- `draft publish`: same flags, confirmation prompt, `--yes` requirement when non-interactive, and the "no pending review comments" error from `glab mr note publish`.
- `draft list` and `draft delete`: the output and prompt behavior designed in !3963.
- `draft update`: the position-preserving update described in #8569 (re-send the existing `position`, because the API clears it otherwise: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/631434).

Removal of the old surface:

- Remove `--draft` from `glab mr note create` and remove `glab mr note publish`, with no deprecation period. Both are marked `(EXPERIMENTAL)`, and the help text states that experimental features "might be unstable or removed at any time." Call out the removal in the MR and release notes.
- Do not add `--draft` to `mr note list`, `mr note delete`, or `mr note update`.

### Further details

Implementation notes:

- Put the commands in their own package (for example `internal/commands/mr/note/draft/`), registered from `NewCmdNote` in `internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note.go` in place of `NewCmdPublish`.
- Move the `--file`/`--line`/`--old-line` → `gitlab.PositionOptions` resolution currently inline in `mr_note_create.go` `complete` into a helper shared by `mr note create` and `mr note draft create`. `mrutils.BuildDiffPosition` and `mrutils.ResolveDiscussionID` are already shared.
- Move `mr_note_publish.go`, its unit tests, and `Test_MrNotePublish_Integration` to the new package. The integration test currently creates its fixture with `NewCmdCreate` and `--draft`, so switch it to `draft create`.
- Run `make gen-docs`. It generates `docs/source/mr/note/draft/*.md`, prunes `docs/source/mr/note/publish.md`, updates `docs/navigation-glab.yaml`, and removes the `--draft` section from `docs/source/mr/note/create.md`.
- Keep `text.ExperimentalString` on every new command.

Effect on in-flight work:

- !3963 (@adityaswarupparida): retarget from `list --draft` / `delete --draft` to `draft list` / `draft delete`. The printing and prompt logic carries over. Only the command wiring and flag-conflict code changes.
- #8569: retarget to `draft update`.

Out of scope:

- Publishing a single draft note (`PUT /draft_notes/:id/publish`). `draft publish` keeps the bulk "submit review" semantics.
- Exposing the draft-notes `resolve_discussion` field ("resolve this thread when the review publishes").

Open question: should the noun be `draft`, matching the API and the original proposal, or `review`, matching the UI's "Start a review" and "Submit review"? This issue proposes `draft`.

### Links / references

- Design discussion: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3885#note_3928426677
- `create --draft`: !3885
- `publish`: !3909
- Pending review workflow tracking: #8560
- List and discard: #8563, !3963
- Edit: #8569
- Original POC: !2932, epic https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/21295
- Prior art: https://gitlab.com/viktomas/note
- Draft notes API: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/draft_notes/

items.title: `glab label list` header shows the page count as the total
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: `glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)`, and reproduced with a build of `main` at 59ae78ca (newer than v1.120.0)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64 (NixOS)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 19.3.3-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output
  (see "Relevant logs" below: debug mode logs only the Git calls, and the
  request itself succeeds)

### Summary

`glab label list` prints the number of labels on the current page as both the
count and the total, so the header never shows the real total. With the
default page size, a project with 33 labels reports `Showing label 30 of 30`,
which looks like a complete list.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64
- SHELL: /run/current-system/sw/bin/zsh
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)

Other: also reproduced with `glab DEV ()` built from `main` at 59ae78ca.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a project (or group) with more labels than one page. The project
   below has 33 labels: `glab api -i "projects/:id/labels?per_page=30"`
   returns `X-Total: 33` and `X-Total-Pages: 2`.
2. Run `glab label list`.
3. Run `glab label list -p 2`, `glab label list -P 10`, and
   `glab label list -g <group>`.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The second number always equals the first one:

```plaintext
$ glab label list
Showing label 30 of 30 on OWNER/REPO.
$ glab label list -p 2
Showing label 3 of 3 on OWNER/REPO.
$ glab label list -P 10
Showing label 10 of 10 on OWNER/REPO.
$ glab label list -g GROUP
Showing label 30 of 30 for group GROUP.
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The second number is the total reported by the API:

```plaintext
Showing label 30 of 33 on OWNER/REPO.
Showing label 3 of 33 on OWNER/REPO.
Showing label 10 of 33 on OWNER/REPO.
Showing label 30 of 33 for group GROUP.
```

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

`GLAB_DEBUG=true` adds no output for this command. `DEBUG=true` logs only
the Git calls, so the debug output does not show anything about the header:

```plaintext
$ DEBUG=true glab label list -p 2
[git remote -v]
[git config --get-regexp ^remote\..*\.glab-resolved(-base|-head)?$]
Showing label 3 of 3 on OWNER/REPO.

ID	Name	Description	Color
...
```

The table body and the JSON output (`-F json`) are correct. Only the header
line is affected.

### Possible fixes

`internal/commands/label/list/label_list.go` passes `len(labels)` twice and
discards the API response:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/59ae78ca/internal/commands/label/list/label_list.go#L145
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/59ae78ca/internal/commands/label/list/label_list.go#L166

Keeping the `*gitlab.Response` from `ListLabels` / `ListGroupLabels` and
printing `resp.TotalItems` fixes it, falling back to the page count when the
response carries no total (GitLab omits `X-Total` for very large result sets).
I have a fix with tests ready and will open a merge request.

Related: #1165 covers list commands that print no total at all. This issue is
narrower: `label list` prints a total, but the wrong one.

items.title: Local configuration overrides glab-managed keys that glab writes only globally
items.body:
### Problem to solve

A repository's local configuration (`.git/glab-cli/config.yml`) can override keys that glab sets automatically, but glab writes those keys only to the global configuration. A stale local value then wins on every read, while every write goes to a file that's never read.

For the Duo CLI, this makes `glab duo cli update` download the same version on every run in that repository:

```plaintext
$ glab duo cli update
Update available: 9.5.0 → 9.26.0
Downloading duo-darwin-arm64 version 9.26.0...
✓ Successfully updated to version 9.26.0
$ glab duo cli update
Update available: 9.5.0 → 9.26.0
...
```

The local file held `duo_cli_binary_version: "9.5.0"`, probably left over from simulating an old install. `binarymgr.Runner.SaveBinaryInfo` writes `9.26.0` to `~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml`, but the next run reads `9.5.0` from the local file again.

`glab config set` writes to the local file by default inside a repository. That's the easy way to end up here: `glab config set duo_cli_binary_version 9.5.0` run in a checkout.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q
export GLAB_CONFIG_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
glab config set duo_cli_binary_version 9.5.0            # writes .git/glab-cli/config.yml
glab config set --global duo_cli_binary_version 9.26.0
glab config get duo_cli_binary_version                  # 9.5.0
```

### Affected keys

The keys described as "automatically set" in `internal/config/schema.go`:

- `duo_cli_binary_path`, `duo_cli_binary_version`, `duo_cli_binary_checksum`, `duo_cli_last_update_check`
- `orbit_cli_binary_path`, `orbit_cli_binary_version`, `orbit_cli_binary_checksum`, `orbit_cli_last_update_check`
- the post-upgrade banner and `glab whatsnew` version keys

`Scope: ScopeGlobal` doesn't cover this. It means "not per host", and ordinary `ScopeGlobal` keys such as `git_protocol` and `branch_prefix` are meant to be set per repository.

### Proposal

Add a `KeyDef` attribute (for example `GlobalOnly`) for glab-managed state, and set it on the keys above. For those keys:

1. Reads skip the local configuration.
2. `glab config set` without `--global` writes them to the global file, or rejects the local write with an error that names `--global`.

Either change alone breaks the loop. Doing both also stops new local values from being written.

### Related

- `glab config get --global` registers `--global` but never reads it (`internal/commands/config/get/config_get.go`), so in the reproduction above it also returns `9.5.0`. Worth a separate fix.
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8568: local config is not shared across Git worktrees.
- Found while reviewing https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3981.

thread.title: Add a way to close milestones
thread.body:
### Problem to solve

Right now you can do the basic CRUD operations on milestones, but you can not close them.

### Proposal

Add a new flag: `glab milestone edit XXX --close` that would close the given milestone.

### Further details

Our milestones work on a time based, so whenever the period finishes, we create new milestones, move open work items to the these new milestones and finally we close the old milestones.

So far we can do all of it but the last part, closing milestones.

### Links / references

items.body:
This is already supported: `glab milestone edit <id> --state close` closes a milestone, and `--state activate` reopens it. It works for project milestones and, with `--group`, for group milestones. It shipped in v1.77.0 via !2536 ([flag definition](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/commands/milestone/edit/edit.go#L85), [docs](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/milestone/edit.md)). Closing as already implemented.

If you think this should remain open or be revisited, please let us know.

readme.content:
# GLab

![GLab](docs/source/img/glab-logo.png)

GLab is an open source GitLab CLI tool. It brings GitLab to your terminal, next to where you are already working with `git` and your code, without switching between windows and browser tabs. While it's powerful for issues and merge requests, `glab` does even more:

- View, manage, and retry CI/CD pipelines directly from your CLI.
- Create changelogs.
- Create and manage releases.
- Ask GitLab Duo Chat (Classic) questions about Git.
- Manage GitLab agents for Kubernetes.

`glab` is available for repositories hosted on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab Self-Managed. It supports multiple authenticated GitLab instances, and automatically detects the authenticated hostname from the remotes available in your working Git directory.

![command example](docs/source/img/getting-started.gif)

## Table of contents

- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Usage](#usage)
  - [Commands](#commands)
  - [GitLab Duo for the CLI](#gitlab-duo-for-the-cli)
- [Demo](#demo)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Installation](#installation)
  - [Homebrew](#homebrew)
  - [Other installation methods](#other-installation-methods)
  - [Building from source](#building-from-source)
    - [Prerequisites for building from source](#prerequisites-for-building-from-source)
- [Authentication](#authentication)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Environment variables](#environment-variables)
  - [Debugging](#debugging)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Issues](#issues)
- [Security](#security)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
  - [Versioning](#versioning)
  - [Classify version changes](#classify-version-changes)
  - [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Inspiration](#inspiration)

## Requirements

`glab` officially supports GitLab versions 16.0 and later. Certain commands might require
more recent versions. While many commands might work properly in GitLab versions
15.x and earlier, no support is provided for these versions.

## Usage

To get started with `glab`:

1. Follow the [installation instructions](#installation) appropriate for your operating system.
1. [Authenticate](#authentication) into your instance of GitLab.
1. Optional. Configure `glab` further to meet your needs:
   - 1Password users can configure it to [authenticate to `glab`](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/shell-plugins/gitlab/).
   - Set any needed global, per-project, or per-host [configuration](#configuration).
   - Set any needed [environment variables](#environment-variables).

You're ready!

### Commands

Run `glab --help` to view a list of core commands in your terminal.

<!-- commands-list-start: generated by 'make gen-docs'; do not edit by hand -->
- [`glab alias`](docs/source/alias): Create, list, and delete aliases.
- [`glab api`](docs/source/api): Make an authenticated request to the GitLab API.
- [`glab artifact-registry`](docs/source/artifact-registry): Authenticate with GitLab Artifact Registry. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab attestation`](docs/source/attestation): Manage software attestations. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab auth`](docs/source/auth): Manage authentication for glab.
- [`glab changelog`](docs/source/changelog): Generate changelogs from your project's commit history.
- [`glab check-update`](docs/source/check-update): Check for the latest glab version.
- [`glab ci`](docs/source/ci): Work with GitLab CI/CD pipelines and jobs.
- [`glab cluster`](docs/source/cluster): Manage GitLab Agents for Kubernetes and their clusters.
- [`glab completion`](docs/source/completion): Generate shell completion scripts.
- [`glab config`](docs/source/config): Manage glab settings.
- [`glab container-registry`](docs/source/container-registry): Work with GitLab container registries.
- [`glab dependency-firewall`](docs/source/dependency-firewall): Configure and monitor GitLab Dependency Firewall for local package managers. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab deploy-key`](docs/source/deploy-key): Manage deploy keys.
- [`glab duo`](docs/source/duo): Work with GitLab Duo.
- [`glab govern`](docs/source/govern): Manage AI agent governance. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab gpg-key`](docs/source/gpg-key): Manage GPG keys registered with your GitLab account.
- [`glab incident`](docs/source/incident): Work with GitLab incidents.
- [`glab issue`](docs/source/issue): Work with GitLab issues.
- [`glab iteration`](docs/source/iteration): Retrieve iteration information.
- [`glab job`](docs/source/job): Work with GitLab CI/CD jobs.
- [`glab label`](docs/source/label): Manage project and group labels.
- [`glab mcp`](docs/source/mcp): Work with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab milestone`](docs/source/milestone): Manage group or project milestones.
- [`glab mr`](docs/source/mr): Create, view, and manage merge requests.
- [`glab opentofu`](docs/source/opentofu): Work with the OpenTofu or Terraform integration.
- [`glab orbit`](docs/source/orbit): Run the Orbit CLI. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab packages`](docs/source/packages): Manage packages in the GitLab package registry.
- [`glab release`](docs/source/release): Manage GitLab releases.
- [`glab repo`](docs/source/repo): Work with GitLab repositories and projects.
- [`glab runner`](docs/source/runner): Manage GitLab CI/CD runners.
- [`glab runner-controller`](docs/source/runner-controller): Manage runner controllers. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab schedule`](docs/source/schedule): Work with GitLab CI/CD schedules.
- [`glab search`](docs/source/search): Search for code and resources in a GitLab project. (BETA)
- [`glab securefile`](docs/source/securefile): Manage secure files for a project.
- [`glab security`](docs/source/security): Manage GitLab security scan profiles for a project. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab skills`](docs/source/skills): Manage glab agent skills. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab snippet`](docs/source/snippet): Create snippets.
- [`glab ssh-key`](docs/source/ssh-key): Manage SSH keys registered with your GitLab account.
- [`glab stack`](docs/source/stack): Create, manage, and work with stacked diffs. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab todo`](docs/source/todo): Manage your to-do list.
- [`glab token`](docs/source/token): Manage personal, project, or group tokens.
- [`glab user`](docs/source/user): Interact with a GitLab user account.
- [`glab variable`](docs/source/variable): Manage variables for a GitLab project or group.
- [`glab version`](docs/source/version): Show version information for glab.
- [`glab whatsnew`](docs/source/whatsnew): Show release notes for new versions of glab.
- [`glab work-items`](docs/source/work-items): Manage work items. (EXPERIMENTAL)
<!-- commands-list-end -->

Commands follow this pattern:

```shell
glab <command> <subcommand> [flags]
```

Many core commands also have sub-commands. Some examples:

- List merge requests assigned to you: `glab mr list --assignee=@me`
- List review requests for you: `glab mr list --reviewer=@me`
- Approve a merge request: `glab mr approve 235`
- Create an issue, and add milestone, title, and label: `glab issue create -m release-2.0.0 -t "My title here" --label important`

### GitLab Duo for the CLI

The GitLab CLI also includes support for using the GitLab Duo Agent Platform directly in your terminal.

Use `glab duo cli` to ask GitLab Duo questions about your codebase and to autonomously perform actions on your behalf.

For more information, see [GitLab Duo CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo_cli/).

## Demo

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/368622.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/368622)

## Documentation

Read the [documentation](docs/source/_index.md) for usage instructions or check out `glab help`.

## Installation

Download a binary suitable for your OS at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases).
Other installation methods depend on your operating system.

### Homebrew

Homebrew is the officially supported package manager for macOS, Linux, and Windows (through [Windows Subsystem for Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install))

- Homebrew
  - Install with: `brew install glab`
  - Update with: `brew upgrade glab`

### Other installation methods

Other options to install the GitLab CLI that may not be officially supported or are maintained by the community are [also available](docs/installation_options.md).

### Building from source

If a supported binary for your OS is not found at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases), you can build from source:

#### Prerequisites for building from source

- `make`
- Go version as defined by [`main/go.mod`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/go.mod?ref_type=heads#L3)

To build from source:

1. Run `go version` to verify that you have the minimum required Go version.
   If Go is not installed, see [Download and install](https://go.dev/doc/install).
1. Clone the repository: `git clone https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git`
1. Build the binary: `make build`
1. Install `glab` in `$GOPATH/bin`: `make install`
1. Optional. If `$GOPATH/bin` or `$GOBIN` is not in your `$PATH`,
   run `export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH`.
1. Confirm the installation: `glab version`

## Authentication

To authenticate `glab` with OAuth, a personal access token, or a CI job token, see
[Authenticate with GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/).

## Configuration

For configuration levels, the configuration search order, and platform-specific file
locations, see [Configure the CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/).

For connecting to a GitLab Self-Managed or GitLab Dedicated instance, and for mTLS and
self-signed certificates, see
[Connect to your GitLab instance](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/connection/).

For authenticating proxies, including custom HTTP headers and Google Identity-Aware
Proxy, see [Connect through a proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/proxies/).

## Environment variables

`glab` reads its configuration from environment variables as well as the configuration
file. Every configuration key has a matching variable, and the variable wins over the
stored value. Setting them centrally is a good way to give everyone in an organization
the same setup.

For the full reference, see
[Environment variables](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/#environment-variables).
For how `glab` picks which token to use, see
[Token precedence](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#token-precedence).

### Debugging

When the `GLAB_DEBUG` environment variable is set to `true`, `glab` outputs more logging information, including:

- Underlying Git commands.
- Expanded aliases.
- DNS error details.

## Troubleshooting

For help with common authentication issues, see
[Troubleshooting](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#troubleshooting) in the GitLab CLI documentation.

## Issues

If you have an issue: report it on the [issue tracker](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues)

## Security

To report a security vulnerability in `glab`, follow the process in
the [security policy](SECURITY.md). Please do not open a public issue.

To learn how the project handles dependency updates and container-scanner CVE
reports, see [dependency management](CONTRIBUTING.md#dependency-management)
and [reporting a vulnerability](CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-vulnerability)
in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Contributing

Feel like contributing? That's awesome! We have a [contributing guide](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of conduct](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) to help guide you.

When updating command help text or documentation, follow the
[GitLab CLI documentation style guide](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/cli_styleguide/).

### Versioning

This project follows the [SemVer](https://github.com/semver/semver) specification.

### Classify version changes

- If deleting a command, changing how it behaves, or adding a new **required** flag, the release must use a new `MAJOR` revision.
- If adding a new command or **optional** flag, the release must use a new `MINOR` revision.
- If fixing a bug, the release must use a new `PATCH` revision.

### Compatibility

We do our best to introduce breaking changes only when releasing a new `MAJOR` version.
Unfortunately, there are situations where this is not possible, and we may introduce
a breaking change in a `MINOR` or `PATCH` version. Some of situations where we may do so:

- If a security issue is discovered, and the solution requires a breaking change,
  we may introduce such a change to resolve the issue and protect our users.
- If a feature was not working as intended, and the bug fix requires a breaking change,
  the bug fix may be introduced to ensure the functionality works as intended.
- When feature behavior is overwhelmingly confusing due to a vague specification
  on how it should work. In such cases, we may refine the specification
  to remove the ambiguity, and introduce a breaking change that aligns with the
  refined specification. For an example of this, see
  [merge request 1382](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/1382#note_1686888887).
- Experimental features are not guaranteed to be stable, and can be modified or
  removed without a breaking change.

Breaking changes are a last resort, and we try our best to only introduce them when absolutely necessary.

## Inspiration

The GitLab CLI was adopted from [Clement Sam](https://gitlab.com/profclems) in 2022 to serve as the official CLI of GitLab. Over the years the project has been inspired by both the [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) and [Zaq? Wiedmann's](https://gitlab.com/zaquestion) [lab](https://github.com/zaquestion/lab).

Lab has served as the foundation for many of the GitLab CI/CD commands including `ci view` and `ci trace`.

items.title: Move pending review comments to `glab mr note draft` subcommands
items.body:
### Problem to solve

Pending review comments (draft notes) are currently exposed as a `--draft` flag on the existing `glab mr note` verbs, plus a separate `publish` verb:

| Action | Today | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | `glab mr note create --draft` | Merged in !3885, released in v1.119.0 |
| Publish | `glab mr note publish` | Merged in !3909, released in v1.120.0 |
| List | `glab mr note list --draft` | Proposed in !3963 (#8563) |
| Discard | `glab mr note delete --draft <id>` | Proposed in !3963 (#8563) |
| Edit | `glab mr note update --draft <id>` | Proposed in #8569 |

Draft notes are a different GitLab resource with a different API (`/merge_requests/:iid/draft_notes`, `DraftNotesService` in client-go) than published notes and discussions. Overloading every `mr note` verb with `--draft` has these costs:

- Every verb branches on `--draft` into a separate code path, with its own client calls, output format, and error messages. `create` already has to dispatch `--draft` before `--reply`, and `list`/`delete`/`update` would each need a parallel implementation (!3963 adds `runDraft`, `completeDraft`, and a separate printer).
- Flag matrices grow. `--draft` must be rejected with `--unique`, `--resolvable=false`, and `--internal` on `create`, and with `--type` and `--state` on `list`. Each rule needs validation code, help text, and tests.
- The ID namespace changes under the same command: `glab mr note delete 123 456` deletes note 456, while `glab mr note delete --draft 123 456` deletes draft note 456.
- `--draft` already means "draft merge request" on `glab mr create`, `glab mr update`, and `glab mr list`. `glab mr list --draft` and `glab mr note list --draft` would filter completely different things.
- The publish step lives at `glab mr note publish`, detached from the commands that manage what it publishes.

Discussed in !3885 (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3885#note_3928426677) and agreed by @viktomas, @phikai, and @andrei.zubov. This is the shape used by the original POC (!2932) and by https://gitlab.com/viktomas/note.

### Proposal

Add a `draft` noun under `glab mr note` that owns the full pending review lifecycle, and remove the flag-based commands:

```shell
glab mr note draft create  [<id> | <branch>] [-m <body>] [--file <path> [--line N[:M] | --old-line N]] [--reply <discussion-id>] [--attach <file>]
glab mr note draft list    [<id> | <branch>] [--file <path>] [-F json]
glab mr note draft update  [<id> | <branch>] <draft-note-id> [-m <body>] [--attach <file>]
glab mr note draft delete  [<id> | <branch>] <draft-note-id> [--yes]
glab mr note draft publish [<id> | <branch>] [-m <summary>] [--internal] [--reviewer-state requested_changes|reviewed] [--yes]
```

Mapping from the current and proposed commands:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `glab mr note create --draft` | `glab mr note draft create` |
| `glab mr note publish` | `glab mr note draft publish` |
| `glab mr note list --draft` (!3963) | `glab mr note draft list` |
| `glab mr note delete --draft` (!3963) | `glab mr note draft delete` |
| `glab mr note update --draft` (#8569) | `glab mr note draft update` |

Behavior carried over unchanged:

- `draft create`: same diff targeting (`--file`, `--line`, `--old-line`), same `--reply` prefix resolution, same `--attach` behavior, and the success output stays the bare draft note ID so it can be piped into `draft update` and `draft delete`. Flags that never applied to drafts (`--unique`, `--resolvable`, `--internal`) do not exist on the new command, so their conflict rules and tests go away.
- `draft publish`: same flags, confirmation prompt, `--yes` requirement when non-interactive, and the "no pending review comments" error from `glab mr note publish`.
- `draft list` and `draft delete`: the output and prompt behavior designed in !3963.
- `draft update`: the position-preserving update described in #8569 (re-send the existing `position`, because the API clears it otherwise: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/631434).

Removal of the old surface:

- Remove `--draft` from `glab mr note create` and remove `glab mr note publish`, with no deprecation period. Both are marked `(EXPERIMENTAL)`, and the help text states that experimental features "might be unstable or removed at any time." Call out the removal in the MR and release notes.
- Do not add `--draft` to `mr note list`, `mr note delete`, or `mr note update`.

### Further details

Implementation notes:

- Put the commands in their own package (for example `internal/commands/mr/note/draft/`), registered from `NewCmdNote` in `internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note.go` in place of `NewCmdPublish`.
- Move the `--file`/`--line`/`--old-line` → `gitlab.PositionOptions` resolution currently inline in `mr_note_create.go` `complete` into a helper shared by `mr note create` and `mr note draft create`. `mrutils.BuildDiffPosition` and `mrutils.ResolveDiscussionID` are already shared.
- Move `mr_note_publish.go`, its unit tests, and `Test_MrNotePublish_Integration` to the new package. The integration test currently creates its fixture with `NewCmdCreate` and `--draft`, so switch it to `draft create`.
- Run `make gen-docs`. It generates `docs/source/mr/note/draft/*.md`, prunes `docs/source/mr/note/publish.md`, updates `docs/navigation-glab.yaml`, and removes the `--draft` section from `docs/source/mr/note/create.md`.
- Keep `text.ExperimentalString` on every new command.

Effect on in-flight work:

- !3963 (@adityaswarupparida): retarget from `list --draft` / `delete --draft` to `draft list` / `draft delete`. The printing and prompt logic carries over. Only the command wiring and flag-conflict code changes.
- #8569: retarget to `draft update`.

Out of scope:

- Publishing a single draft note (`PUT /draft_notes/:id/publish`). `draft publish` keeps the bulk "submit review" semantics.
- Exposing the draft-notes `resolve_discussion` field ("resolve this thread when the review publishes").

Open question: should the noun be `draft`, matching the API and the original proposal, or `review`, matching the UI's "Start a review" and "Submit review"? This issue proposes `draft`.

### Links / references

- Design discussion: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3885#note_3928426677
- `create --draft`: !3885
- `publish`: !3909
- Pending review workflow tracking: #8560
- List and discard: #8563, !3963
- Edit: #8569
- Original POC: !2932, epic https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/21295
- Prior art: https://gitlab.com/viktomas/note
- Draft notes API: https://docs.gitlab.com/api/draft_notes/

items.title: Proposal: Use Git Porcelain Format for Stack Sync
items.body:
**Goal:** Replace human-readable Git message parsing with machine-readable porcelain format

## Executive Summary

Using Git's `--porcelain` format is the **best practice** for programmatic Git interaction. This proposal outlines a refactor of `glab stack sync` to use stable, machine-readable Git output instead of parsing human-readable status messages.

## Why Porcelain Format?

### Current Approach Problems

The current implementation parses human-readable Git messages:

```go
const (
    BranchIsBehind    = "Your branch is behind"
    BranchHasDiverged = "have diverged"
    NothingToCommit   = "nothing to commit"
)
```

**Issues:**
1. ❌ **Fragile** - Git could change message wording in future versions
2. ❌ **Locale-dependent** - Requires forcing `LC_ALL=C` workaround
3. ❌ **Substring matching** - Prone to false positives
4. ❌ **Not Git's intended interface** - Goes against Git's design principles

### Porcelain Format Benefits

Git explicitly provides `--porcelain` formats for scripts and tools:

1. ✅ **Stable API** - Git guarantees backward compatibility
2. ✅ **Locale-independent** - Works in any language setting
3. ✅ **Structured data** - Easy to parse accurately
4. ✅ **Git's recommended approach** - Documented for scripting use
5. ✅ **Future-proof** - Won't break with Git updates

From Git documentation:
> "Porcelain format: The output format is stable and designed to be machine-parsable. The format will not change in backward incompatible ways between Git versions."

### Real-World Precedent

Many CLI tools use porcelain formats:
- **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) - Uses porcelain for status checking
- **GitLab Runner** - Uses porcelain in CI/CD scripts
- **Pre-commit hooks** - Standard practice in Git ecosystem

## Technical Design

### Git Status Porcelain v1 Format

The `--porcelain=v1` format provides structured output:

```bash
$ git status --porcelain=v1 -b -uno
## main...origin/main [ahead 1, behind 2]
```

**Format breakdown:**
- `##` - Branch header line
- `main` - Current branch name
- `...origin/main` - Upstream tracking branch
- `[ahead 1, behind 2]` - Tracking status (optional)

**Possible tracking states:**
- `[ahead N]` - Local branch is ahead
- `[behind N]` - Local branch is behind
- `[ahead N, behind M]` - Branches have diverged
- *(no bracket)* - Branches are in sync

**Additional status codes** (for working directory):
- ` M file.txt` - Modified file
- `A  file.txt` - Added file
- `D  file.txt` - Deleted file
- `??` - Untracked file (excluded with `-uno`)

### Proposed Implementation

#### 1. Update branchStatus() Function

**File:** [internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go:223-237](internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go#L223-L237)

```go
// Current implementation:
func branchStatus(ref *git.StackRef, gr git.GitRunner) (string, error) {
    checkout, err := gr.Git("checkout", ref.Branch)
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
-   output, err := gr.Git("status", "-uno")
+   output, err := gr.Git("status", "--porcelain=v1", "-b", "-uno")
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    return output, nil
}
```

**Flags:**
- `--porcelain=v1` - Use stable porcelain format version 1
- `-b` - Include branch tracking information
- `-uno` - Don't show untracked files (existing behavior)

#### 2. Create Porcelain Parser

Add a new parsing function to handle porcelain output:

```go
// File: internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go

// BranchTrackingStatus represents the relationship between local and upstream branches
type BranchTrackingStatus int

const (
    StatusUnknown BranchTrackingStatus = iota
    StatusUpToDate
    StatusBehind
    StatusAhead
    StatusDiverged
    StatusNoUpstream
)

// parsePorcelainStatus parses git status --porcelain=v1 -b output
// to determine branch tracking status.
//
// Expected format:
//   ## branch...upstream [ahead N, behind M]
//
// Returns:
//   - StatusBehind: branch is behind upstream
//   - StatusAhead: branch is ahead of upstream
//   - StatusDiverged: branch has diverged from upstream
//   - StatusUpToDate: branch is up to date with upstream
//   - StatusNoUpstream: branch has no upstream configured
//   - StatusUnknown: unable to parse status
func parsePorcelainStatus(porcelainOutput string) BranchTrackingStatus {
    lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(porcelainOutput), "\n")
    if len(lines) == 0 {
        return StatusUnknown
    }

    // First line should be branch header: ## branch...upstream [tracking]
    branchLine := lines[0]
    if !strings.HasPrefix(branchLine, "## ") {
        return StatusUnknown
    }

    // Remove "## " prefix
    branchInfo := strings.TrimPrefix(branchLine, "## ")

    // Check if branch has upstream
    if !strings.Contains(branchInfo, "...") {
        return StatusNoUpstream
    }

    // Extract tracking information (content within brackets)
    trackingStart := strings.Index(branchInfo, "[")
    trackingEnd := strings.Index(branchInfo, "]")

    if trackingStart == -1 || trackingEnd == -1 {
        // No tracking information means branches are in sync
        return StatusUpToDate
    }

    tracking := branchInfo[trackingStart+1 : trackingEnd]

    hasAhead := strings.Contains(tracking, "ahead ")
    hasBehind := strings.Contains(tracking, "behind ")

    switch {
    case hasAhead && hasBehind:
        return StatusDiverged
    case hasBehind:
        return StatusBehind
    case hasAhead:
        return StatusAhead
    default:
        return StatusUpToDate
    }
}
```

+

## Compatibility Considerations

### Git Version Requirements

- `--porcelain=v1` format: Available since Git 1.7.0 (2010)
- `-b` flag: Available since Git 1.8.0 (2012)
- `glab` minimum requirement: Git 2.20+ (already required)

### Backward Compatibility

**User-facing:**

## Performance Impact

### Before (Human-readable parsing)
```bash

  (use "git pull" to update your local branch)

```

### After (Porcelain format)
```bash
$ git status --porcelain=v1 -b -uno

```

**Performance improvement:**
- ⚡ 77% less data to parse
- ⚡ Faster parsing (structured vs. substring matching)
- ⚡ No regex or complex string operations needed

### Risk 1: Porcelain format parsing bugs

### Risk 2: Unexpected Git output variations
**Mitigation:**
- Test with multiple Git versions
- Handle `StatusUnknown` case gracefully
- Add detailed error messages for debugging

### Risk 3: Breaking changes in Git
**Mitigation:**
- Git explicitly guarantees porcelain format stability
- This is less risky than parsing human-readable messages

### 1. Porcelain v2 Format

   - v1: More compatible (Git 1.7.0+)
   - v2: More structured (Git 2.11+)
   - **Recommendation:** Start with v1, migrate to v2 later if needed

2. **Should we create a shared Git parser package?**

## Appendix: Porcelain Format Reference

### Branch Tracking Line Format

```
## <local>...<upstream> [<tracking>]
```

**Components:**
- `##` - Branch line marker (always present)
- `<local>` - Local branch name
- `...` - Separator (present only if upstream exists)
- `<upstream>` - Upstream branch name
- `[<tracking>]` - Tracking status (present only if ahead/behind)

**Tracking formats:**
- `[ahead N]` - Local is N commits ahead
- `[behind N]` - Local is N commits behind
- `[ahead N, behind M]` - Diverged by N ahead, M behind
- *(absent)* - Branches are in sync

### File Status Format

Each subsequent line shows file changes:

```
XY filename
```

**X (index status):**
- `M` - Modified
- `A` - Added
- `D` - Deleted
- `R` - Renamed
- `C` - Copied

**Y (working tree status):**
- `M` - Modified
- `D` - Deleted
- `?` - Untracked (excluded with `-uno`)

**Examples:**
- ` M file.txt` - Modified in working tree
- `M  file.txt` - Modified in index
- `MM file.txt` - Modified in both
- `A  file.txt` - Added to index
- `D  file.txt` - Deleted from index

For our use case, we only care about the branch tracking line (first line).

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

All work is in `internal/commands/stack/sync/`. No user-facing help text changes, so `make gen-docs` is not needed.

1. **Switch the status call to porcelain.** In `branchStatus` (`internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go:346`), change `gr.Git("status", "-uno")` to `gr.Git("status", "--porcelain=v1", "-b", "-uno")`. Leave the `checkout` call and the `dbg.Debug` lines alone.

2. **Add a parser.** In the same file, add an unexported enum and `parseBranchTrackingStatus(output string)`. Read only the first line, require the `## ` prefix, and return: no-upstream when the line has no `...` separator (this also covers `## HEAD (no branch)`), up-to-date when there is no `[...]` segment, and behind / ahead / diverged from the `behind ` and `ahead ` tokens inside the brackets. Anything without the `## ` prefix is unknown. Do not parse the file-status lines; the sync loop does not use them.

3. **Rewrite the dispatch, preserving today's behavior.** Replace the `strings.Contains` switch at `internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go:187-205` with a switch on the parsed status: behind calls `branchBehind`, diverged calls `branchDiverged`, up-to-date falls through. Two cases need care and are the point of the change:
   - No upstream must stay silent and fall through. A fresh stack branch has no upstream until `populateMR` pushes it later in the same loop, so warning here would fire on the normal path.
   - Ahead keeps the existing error text ("your Git branch is ahead, but it shouldn't be; you might need to squash your commits"), and unknown returns a distinct error naming the branch. The proposal's draft turns ahead into a success line; that is a behavior change and should not ride along with the refactor.
   Note that this step fixes a real defect: with porcelain, a clean-tracking branch that has uncommitted modifications is correctly up-to-date, where today it hits the default case and aborts the sync.

4. **Delete the old constants.** Remove `BranchIsBehind`, `BranchHasDiverged` and `NothingToCommit` from the const block at `internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync.go:50-52`, keeping `mergedStatus` and `closedStatus`. Drop the `strings` import if nothing else in the file uses it.

5. **Tests.** In `internal/commands/stack/sync/stack_sync_test.go`, add a table-driven `TestParseBranchTrackingStatus` covering up-to-date, behind, ahead, diverged, a status line followed by a ` M file.txt` line, no upstream, detached HEAD, empty input and garbage input. Then update the existing harness: the mock expectation at line 1061 becomes `Git([]string{"status", "--porcelain=v1", "-b", "-uno"})`, and the `state:` fixtures throughout the file switch from the removed constants to test-local porcelain strings (for example `"## b...origin/b [behind 1]\n"`) that the switch at lines 1063-1072 dispatches on.

items.title: Allow configuring additional OAuth scopes (e.g. admin_mode) for auth login
items.body:
## Problem

The OAuth scopes that `glab` requests during `glab auth login` are hardcoded and cannot be configured by users. They are defined as a fixed package-level slice in [`internal/oauth2/config.go`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/oauth2/config.go):

```go
var scopes = []string{"openid", "profile", "read_user", "write_repository", "api"}
```

Because there is no config key, flag, or environment variable that feeds into this list, OAuth-authenticated sessions can never include scopes beyond these five.

## Impact

Some workflows require admin-only APIs, which need the `admin_mode` scope. Since OAuth sessions in `glab` cannot request `admin_mode` (or any other additional scope), these admin APIs do not work when authenticating via OAuth. Today the only workaround is to fall back to a personal access token with the required scopes, which is less convenient and bypasses the OAuth flow entirely.

## Proposal

Provide a way for users to request additional OAuth scopes (such as `admin_mode`) when authenticating with `glab auth login`, so admin APIs are usable over OAuth.

This issue intentionally stays high level and does not prescribe a specific implementation. Some considerations worth discussing during design:

- The OAuth application registered for the instance must also allow the requested scope, so prerequisites and error messaging should be clear.
- Backward compatibility: default behavior should remain unchanged.
